source_text: Unusquisque autem in suo ordine: primitiae Christus, deinde hi qui sunt Christi in adventu eius, deinde finis [n222] . Idem et alibi: Qui est primogenitus - inquit - ex mortuis [n223] . Deinde hi qui sunt Christi: id est, sancti rapiuntur in nubibus [n224] . Post hoc finis: quoniam hi ibunt in regnum aeternum, impii vero in ignem aeternum [n225] . Cum tradiderit regnum Deo et Patri, cum evacuaverit omnem principatum, et omnem potestatem, et virtutem; oportet enim eum regnare, donec ponat inimicos omnes sub pedibus eius; omnia enim subiecit subtus pedes eius; novissima autem inimica destruetur mors. Cum autem dixerit: Omnia ista subiecta sunt, sine dubio praeter illum qui illi subiecit omnia; nam cum subiecta fuerint illi omnia, tunc et ipse subiectus erit ei qui sibi subiecit omnia, ut sit Deus omnia in omnibus [n226] . Regnum Dei et Patris est, ut impleto numero sanctorum qui in eius praescientia continetur, omnis principatus et universa virtus adversariae potestatis intereat. Oportet quippe hanc efficientiam tanti esse mysterii, ut omnes inimici iustitiae sub divinis pedibus collocentur. Quod tunc fiet, cum destructam se et victam ab omnibus sanctis mors aeterna conspiciet. Cum autem fuerint tam Christo quam corpori eius omnia illa potestatum genera regni manifestatione subiecta, multo maxime congregatio omnis glorificata sanctorum esse Deo subdita non desistet; sed totum corpus dignum regno caelorum, quod sub Christo capite construitur, divinae voluntati perfecta affectione cohaerebit, ut exstincta omni cupiditate culparum, Deus et contineat cunctos, et compleat.
pass_a_gloss: But each one in his own order: firstfruits Christ, then those who are Christ's at his coming, then the end. The same also elsewhere: Who is, he says, firstborn from the dead. Then those who are Christ's: that is, the holy are snatched in clouds. After this the end: because these will go into an eternal kingdom, but the impious into eternal fire. When he shall have handed over the kingdom to God and the Father, when he shall have emptied every principality, and every power, and virtue; for he must reign, until he places all enemies under his feet; for he subjected all things under his feet; but the last enemy death will be destroyed. But when he shall have said: All these things have been subjected, without doubt besides him who subjected all things to him; for when all things shall have been subjected to him, then he himself also will be subjected to him who subjected all things to himself, that God may be all in all. The kingdom of God and of the Father is, that, the number of the holy which is contained in his prescience having been filled, every principality and all virtue of an adversary power may perish. For this efficiency of so great a mystery must be, that all enemies of justice be placed under divine feet. Which will then be done, when eternal death will see itself destroyed and conquered by all the holy. But when all those kinds of powers shall have been subjected both to Christ and to his body by a manifestation of the kingdom, much most the whole glorified congregation of the holy will not desist from being subjected to God; but the whole body worthy of the kingdom of heavens, which is constructed under Christ the head, will cohere to the divine will by a perfect affection, so that, every desire of faults having been extinguished, God both may contain all, and may fill.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: ‘But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then those who belong to Christ at his coming; then the end’ (1 Corinthians 15:23–24). Elsewhere the same apostle says: ‘He is the firstborn from the dead’ (Colossians 1:18). ‘Then those who belong to Christ’: that is, the saints are caught up in the clouds (1 Thessalonians 4:17). After this, the end: these will go into the eternal kingdom, while the ungodly go into eternal fire (Matthew 25:34, 41, 46).

‘When he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he abolishes every rule and every authority and power—for he must reign until he puts all enemies under his feet; he has subjected everything beneath his feet—the last enemy, death, will be destroyed. When he says, Everything has been subjected, this plainly excludes the one who subjected everything to him. When everything has been subjected to him, then he himself will also be subject to the one who subjected everything to him, so that God may be all in all’ (1 Corinthians 15:24–28).

The kingdom of God the Father means that, when the number of saints contained in his foreknowledge is complete, every dominion and all the strength of hostile power will perish. The effect of so great a mystery must be to place all justice’s enemies beneath divine feet. This will happen when eternal death sees itself destroyed and defeated by all the saints.

When all those kinds of powers have been subjected to Christ and his body through the kingdom’s manifestation, the whole glorified congregation of saints will most certainly never cease to be subject to God. The entire body worthy of the kingdom of heaven, built under Christ as head, will cling to the divine will with perfect love, so that, with every desire for faults extinguished, God may both embrace and fill everyone.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
